messages:
alex: Heads up — saw a perf regression and a couple OOMs on long sequences (seq=4096) in production today. Latency spike + occasional OOMs when FlashAttention is chosen for attention and Triton FFN allocates a big workspace.

maria: Ugh. Any profiling info? is it the allocator not releasing between kernels or just workspace sizing heuristics? :thinking:

alex: Quick profiler dump attached (summarized):
```
PROFILE SUMMARY: run_id=2026-03-17
total_tokens: 1.2M
median_latency_per_token: 12.8ms
attention (FlashAtt): avg_time=47ms, workspace=1.3GB
ffn (Triton): avg_time=62ms, workspace=900MB
alloc/free churn: many transient peaks ~2.4GB
OOMs: 3 (nvml OOM) during burst of concurrent requests
```
Seems like peaks > device mem when multiple requests hit and allocator fails to reuse transient buffers.

sam: Are we still using a single global arena for all temp workspaces? I remember we had an experiment to split arenas by kernel type.

kevin: Yes — current allocator is arena-based but allocation sizes are quite varied; fragmentation + worst-case workspace requests cause peaks. Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) hard cap per-kernel workspace budget at runtime and fall back to cuBLASLt/naive FFN when Flash/Triton can't get the budget; 2) introduce a transient buffer pool keyed by (kernel_family, max_seq_len_bin) to enable reuse.

maya: For (1) we need good heuristics to pick the fallback. FlashAttention is great for long heads but terrible if workspace is constrained. I'd propose: prefer FlashAttn when seq_len * head_dim >= 256k AND free_device_mem >= 1.1x estimated_workspace. Otherwise pick the cuBLASLt attention path.

alex: That sounds sensible. For FFN: Triton kernels have multiple tiling configs. We currently pick the fastest overall config, but the one with best latency often needs bigger workspace. Could we switch selection objective to minimize peak combined workspace across attention+ffn?

maria: Yes — selection should be joint. We can compute an estimated combined workspace per-request: W_attn(seq, config) + W_ffn(seq, config). Then choose kernel pair minimizing latency subject to W_total < budget. Budget could be static (e.g., 60% of device mem) or dynamic (mem - reserved_for_kv).

sam: Speaking of KV: remember that persistent KV cache is the big resident chunk. On long chat sessions the KV cache grows and reduces headroom. We should factor resident_kv into the available workspace budget. E.g., avail = total_mem - resident_kv - reserved_margin.

kevin: Implementation sketch:
```
config.runtime.workspace_budgets = {
  global_pct: 0.6,               # max fraction of device mem for transient workspace
  per_kernel_max: {
    flash_attn: 1<<30,           # 1GB hard cap
    triton_ffn: 1<<29            # 512MB hard cap
  },
  reserve_for_kv_pct: 0.25      # keep 25% for resident KV by default
}
```
Allocator changes: make transient_pool keyed by (kernel, seq_bin) and reuse buffers if size within 8%. If no buffer, allocate but track budgets atomically.

maria: Could also add a small padding strategy: pad sequences to power-of-two bins to improve reuse across requests and reduce fragmentation. That trades a bit of extra resident KV/compute for lower allocator churn.

alex: We tried padding in staging — it reduced allocator churn but increased token compute by ~3%. For latency-sensitive workloads that was acceptable. Patch notes: padding to 256-boundary bins gave best reuse.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline: run perf-suite/long-seq (3x) — queued.

sam: Another thing — add a fallback circuit: if combined_estimated_work > budget, route request to a slower model variant with smaller d_model or lower head_dim, or trigger model-quantization on-the-fly. That keeps latency predictable instead of OOM.

kevin: Agreed. Also we should add a cheap pre-check in the fast path: compute combined_estimated_work BEFORE allocating KV or transient buffers. If it fails, early fallback. Helps avoid partial allocation state leading to OOM.

maria: For offline testing I'm going to run a grid over: seq_len in {512,1024,2048,4096}, batch in {1,2,4}, head_dim in {64,128}, and both allocator modes (global arena vs per-kernel pool). I'll log: peak_mem, fragmentation metric, failures, and p95 lat.

alex: Can you add a column for mem_reservation_by_kv as well? We need to see interaction.

maria: Yep. Also adding a column for "chosen_kernel_pair" so we can correlate config to outcomes.

sam: Small ops-level idea: after attention completes we currently immediately allocate FFN workspace. Instead, try reusing attention workspace for FFN temporaries if size and lifetime allow. That requires aligning strides and tile layouts but could cut peak by one large allocation.

kevin: Nice — that's buffer aliasing. We'll need kernel-level support: provide an API for a kernel to declare "I can accept a preallocated workspace buffer if it meets size/alignment/tile constraints". Then allocator can hand the previous buffer instead of new alloc.

maya: For Triton kernels we might need to add a bit in kernel launcher metadata: preferred alignment and pitch, and a fallback path if buffer format mismatch.

alex: Next steps:
- maria: run grid and upload CSV to /perf/attn-ffn/workspace-grid-17921.csv
- kevin: prototype transient_pool + per_kernel_budget feature branch (alloc/pr 4689)
- sam: prototype pre-check combined_estimation and early-fallback router
- maya: evaluate padding bins tradeoffs on perf-suite

maria: will start runs now. tagging results here when done. :rocket:

kevin: I'll open alloc PR with unit tests for pool reuse and an integration test simulating concurrent small requests + one big request to reproduce previous OOM.

alex: Thanks team. If anyone hits the infra-bot failures ping me and I'll reprioritize the perf runners.

maya: Quick note — consider exposing a runtime flag for customers to prefer throughput over latency (which toggles global_pct/perc_kernel caps). Some customers might accept slower kernel choices to reduce costs/avoid OOMs.

alex: Good UX call. We'll add that config to route-level settings.

infra-bot: perf-suite/long-seq run completed: 3/3 OK, artifacts at s3://redwood-perf/attn-ffn/1792103456/

maria: Uploading preliminary CSV now. I'll post summary after parsing. """
